claims.explanation: Atorvastatin's selective killing likely reflects dependence on the mevalonate/cholesterol synthesis pathway, with sensitive lines showing intact HMGCR-pathway activity and/or loss of negative feedback, while resistant lines tolerate statin-induced HMGCR inhibition. The strongest recurrent genomic pattern among sensitive lines is PTEN mutation/loss, which can activate PI3K-AKT-mTOR and increase demand for mevalonate-derived lipids; TP53 mutation is common but not selective. Additional sensitivity may come from HRAS/BRAF/MAPK activation and SMARCA4 loss, whereas protective features include PIK3CA mutation, CDKN2A loss, and NF1 mutation in the resistant set.

features.basis: Recurrent damaging PTEN mutations in sensitive lines; PI3K-AKT activation increases mevalonate pathway demand
Atorvastatin directly inhibits HMGCR; higher pathway dependence predicts greater killing
Hotspot HRAS mutations enriched in sensitive lines; MAPK activation may increase lipid synthesis demand
Hotspot BRAF mutations in several sensitive lines; MAPK-driven proliferation may depend on mevalonate flux
Damaging SMARCA4 mutations recurrent in sensitive lines; chromatin remodeling loss may alter sterol response
Damaging EGFR mutations in sensitive lines; RTK-driven growth may increase mevalonate pathway activity
PIK3CA mutations more common in resistant lines; constitutive PI3K may bypass statin-induced growth suppression
CDKN2A loss frequent in resistant lines; cell-cycle deregulation may reduce dependence on mevalonate-derived signals
NF1 mutations in resistant lines; RAS-MAPK activation without lipid dependency may confer tolerance
TP53 mutations common in both groups but enriched in resistant lines; loss may reduce statin-induced apoptosis
KRAS mutations present in resistant colorectal and pancreatic lines; may sustain growth independent of mevalonate
Annotated atorvastatin target; AHR activity may modulate drug response
